Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

legislation noun

also legislate, law-making, pass a law, pass legislation, propose a law, legislator, lawmaker

classical

Hor. Ep. 2.1.3: lēgibus ēmendēs
Traupman 179

lēgēs, lēgum f. pl.

plural of lēx, lēgis f., declension

laws, legislation

Latin speaks of laws, not of legislation. To propose a law is lēgem ferre (Traupman 180), to carry it lēgem perferre (Traupman 179), to vote it down antīquāre (Cic. Off. 2.73; Traupman 180); for the single law, see law.

Other words

  • lēgis lātor (lēgum lātor), lēgis lātōris m. — a legislator, the proposer of a law

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 4.10: lātor lēgis Semprōniae (Lewis & Short, s.v. lātor); Liv. 34.31 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 179

    Classical authors write it as two words (Lewis & Short); Traupman prints lēgislātor, which Valerius Maximus and the jurists use.

  • lēgislātiō, lēgislātiōnis f. — legislation

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Rom. 9.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 339

    Traupman’s word; anciently found once, in the Vulgate, for the giving of the Law to Israel (Lewis & Short).

  • lēgislātor, lēgislātōris m. — legislator

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Traupman 179

    Classical Latin writes it as two words, lēgis lātor.

Examples

  • Perniciōsē enim Philippus in tribūnātū cum lēgem agrāriam ferret, quam tamen antīquārī facile passus est

    Philippus did harm when, as tribune, he proposed a land law, though he readily let it be voted downCic. Off. 2.73

See also law, parliament, vote.
